lines.en: It’s easy to forget sometimes because of all the bullshit, but there’s an entire world with people in it that are doing stuff right now, and I think that’s pretty cool.
For example, while you’re off ironing your socks or organizing hot dog buns like regular people do, there’s someone in Iran or something hitting the Griddy, completely unaware of your existence.
What is the “Griddy” you ask? I don’t know. Something young people do, I think. Or did. Keeping up with the Joneses is quite difficult when they’re spread out across various timelines.
But the point I’m trying to make here is simple. It’s that the world still moves without you. And once you stop moving, it’s not like it’s going to just follow your lead.
Or maybe it will. And maybe Matt Damon was right when he wrote that thing about eggs in Project Hail Mary. Maybe you’re not you and you’re actually me and we’re all just us together?
Whatever the case, I think you should live each day knowing that it could be the last chance you ever get to hit the Griddy.
Here’s looking at you, Casablanca.
: Did Otoha really write this?...
: It’s, like...actually good...
: It’s easy to forget because Nodoka exists, but Otoha’s a creative genius as well. You should have seen some of the stuff she was coming up with in our old school.
: Is that...why she was so popular over there?...
: No. Well, maybe a little. I think it was just mostly because she’s hot and cool and wears a lot of rings.
: You guys know I can hear you, right? You’re not even trying to whisper.
: Otoha, how many of these songs are about my sister?
: Uhh, none?! What?! Why would you...how did you...
: It’s kind of obvious once you know Niki as a person.
: You keep referencing things about her that only people like me, Sensei, and I guess you would understand. It’s cute. I never realized how bad you were down for her before.
: I’m not “down bad” at all! It’s probably just a coincidence!
: I’m confused. Why would Sensei be familiar with Niki? That doesn’t make any sense.
: Chika, come on. Has it really not clicked yet or are you just being delusional on purpose?
: Has what not clicked yet? What are you talking about? Also, as the admin of her third most popular fanpage, chances are I know just as much about her as-
: Hi! So, now that practice is finally over, can you please just-
: AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
: J-J-J-J-J-J-JUST REMEMBERED I HAVE TO...SHOES! BYE!
: Oh, come on! What good is “see you in school” if you’re just going to do this every time we’re here!
: CAN’T HEAR YOU! SHOES!
: YOU CAN’T RUN FROM ME FOREVER, CHOSOKABE! I WILL FIND YOU!
: What’s going on with Chika? Why does she need to “shoes” so urgently?
: She’s just embarrassed after finally shooting her shot with Rin only to have the gun misfire and take her whole fucking hand off.
: “Shoot your shot” is a reference to basketball. There are no guns involved, Otoha.
: Basketball’s an American sport, isn’t it? There are probably guns involved. We just don’t know about them.
: There goes Otoha and her racism again...
: Stop calling me a racist! My teacher is black!
: I see...So Chika finally shot her shot with Rin...and the gun misfired...
: (Computing)
: (Still computing)
: Psst. I think it’s your line.
: Wait! Chika confessed to you and you turned her down?!?!?! And I didn’t know about it?!?!?!
: If you don’t want to tell me because I’m your mom, fine! But at least have the courtesy to tell me as your club advisor!
: I don’t want to do either of those things! I can handle this on my own and you’re just going to make it weird!
: But I can make it weird in the hallway! I don’t have to do it in front of your friends!
: Mom, stop! This is hard enough without you breathing down my neck about it!
: Tell me what happened and I’ll give you your phone back!
: Hallway. Now.
: Daughter.
: Mother...
: Tell me the tales of your lesbian woes so that I can help you and feel better about mine.
: They’re not really woes at all...Chika just told me she likes me and that she can’t hang out with me anymore because of it.
: What? Why? Is it like another Otoha thing where she just doesn’t want her parents to find out?
: Otoha lied about that, Mom. She was the one embarrassed, not her parents. Also, Chika doesn’t have parents. Remember?
: Two things: shame on Otoha, condolences to Chika.
: Why can’t she hang out with you though? You guys have been inseparable lately. I already started planning the wedding.
: Where?! Gay marriage isn’t legal here!
: First rule of lesbians, Rin — there is always a hole. In this case a loophole. I’ll figure it out. Just worry about filling the hole. The other one. Without the loop.
: Mom, I don’t like Chika like that anymore! I just want her to keep being my friend because I miss her and care about her!
: Rin...you liked her for years. I know those feelings aren’t just gone. What happened?
: Did you reject her? Is that why she can’t hang out with you? Will she if you accept? Do you not even want to try?
: I do but...there’s...
: There’s somebody else I like more, okay?
: What? Who? Noriko? I bet it’s Noriko. You guys would be adorable together. Or maybe Sana! A little small, sure. But I get it.
: It’s no one from the club, mom.
: Molly. Futaba. God, I hope it’s not Futaba. She’s too sweet for this family. Yumi! Uhh...Touka! You’re a gold digger! Don’t do it, Rin!
: It’s no one from class either, Mom. Or school in general.
: Don’t tell me you like Noriko’s sister too. What’s Otoha going to think?
: What does that stare mean? You know I’m bad with interpreting facial expressions.
: I’m just waiting for you to figure it out since I think it’d be kind of obvious given somewhat recent developments.
: Recent developments...
: (Computing)
: I’m hungry. Can I run to the vending machine while your brain is stuck loading?
: Rin...you’re not talking about Sensei again, are you?
: Ding ding ding. Turns out taking my phone away didn’t magically cure me of liking him. Who would’ve thought?
: It wasn’t supposed to cure you! But I figured that him letting you down and telling you he wasn’t interested in girls your age would have been all you needed to move on!
: Oh. Right. Yeah. He definitely did that. And it was completely natural and didn’t make me suspect you had anything to do with it at all.
: And it changed nothing?! You still like him? He’s old enough to be your father...ish.
: Hey, maybe he is? It’s not like we actually know. And it’s not like even that would change anything at this point given how I’ve already made up my mind.
: So...you’ve made up your mind to the point where finding out he’s your biological father still wouldn’t make you reconsider?
: I don’t know. It works for Ami, doesn’t it?
: Does it?
: Sometimes. When she’s not threatening to kill us.
: Rin, I’m not okay with this. And neither is Akira. And I get that your feelings are strong, but all you’re doing by continuing to go after him is making things harder for both of you.
: Isn’t that good, though? Won’t it just make me stronger if I wind up getting hurt again? Like what happened with Chika and Otoha. And even you with Mom.
: I am a lot of things without your mother, but “strong” is not one of them.
: You’re holding down a job. You have your own apartment now. You’ve even learned how to do laundry.
: Mostly. I still need Imani’s help with that sometimes.
: Okay, fine. Then you’re almost capable of doing laundry. But you’re still in a much better spot now than you were a few years ago.
: Not mentally. Or physically for that matter. Just in status alone, and that doesn’t make me stronger, it just helps hide me from criticism.
: So what’s the moral here then? Know when to quit? Is that what you’re trying to teach me?
: I didn’t have a specific moral in mind but yeah, that sounds good. Know when to quit.
: Seems contradictory to the “never give up” message I’ve gotten in the past.
: Know when to quit but never give up. Sounds like a good yearbook quote. Do I get a yearbook quote? Don’t take that. I want to use it.
: Mom, I don’t care how many times you tell Sensei to turn me down. I still like him enough to not want anyone else, and there’s nothing you can do to change that.
: You don’t know it was me who told him to do that. He could have decided that on his own. Which he probably did because that would be what a smart person does and he is a smart person.
: It was definitely you who told him to do that. Sensei doesn’t “let people down,” Mom. He lets them drown in uncertainty forever because it’s easier than openly hurting them.
: I know this because I’ve watched him for so long. He’s my best friend. And it’s okay that you think that’s weird, but nothing has happened between us. And that pisses me off.
: So maybe I just need to be pissed off a little longer. Maybe that’s what will get me to rethink romance and fall back on Chika or Noriko or any of the people you want me to be with.
: But do you know what I have to say about that, Mom? About you thinking you can exercise this sort of authority to guide me down that path you want me to take?
: What?...What do you think?...
: I think...
: That’s not punk at all and you’re just a big loser! Beeeeeeh!
: Wha- where do you get off, young lady?!
: Hopefully Sensei’s house! Phbhbhbhhtt!!!!
: I’m hanging onto your phone! You’re not getting it back now!
: I already picked your pocket while you were lecturing me because I’m not a poser! Later, Mom!
: What the-
: God damn it. That was so fucking cool.
: Imani, we have a problem. My daughter says I’m not punk anymore.
: Aren’t you a little too old to be fighting back against the establishment anyway? Maybe this is the wake-up call you need.
: Also, she wants to fuck Akira.
: So do you. And honestly, I’m surprised you haven’t yet.
: Sure, but maybe he wants to fuck her too!
: Wanting to and actually doing it are two different things. Do you have any proof that this has actually happened?
: No. In fact, Rin has confirmed to me that it has not.
: Great. So you have a horny daughter. I don’t see how this is my problem at all.
: The problem is that I told Akira to let Rin down so that she wouldn’t keep pursuing him and I don’t think he actually did!
: Well, yeah. Senpai doesn’t “let people down.” He lets them drown in uncertainty forever because it’s easier than openly hurting them.
: GOD FUCKING DAMN IT! ARE WE EVEN FRIENDS?! WHY DOES EVERYONE KNOW THIS BUT ME?!
: Is there anything else or can I get back to grading papers now?
: Imani, when I was in ninth grade, the whole school started spreading rumors about me giving this dude named Take a handjob in the locker room. It lasted all the way until graduation.
: Well...did you?
: Yes! But that’s exactly the problem! Word doesn’t get around this intensely unless there’s some semblance of truth to it!
: So if everyone is trying to jump Akira’s bones, which we clearly see they are, and he’s not turning them down, shouldn’t we be suspicious about that?!
: You’re just now catching onto all of this?
: Have you been suspicious the entire time then?! Has everyone?! What have we done about it?!
: Hah...what can we do about it other than wait for somebody to slip up?
: I obviously want to give Senpai the benefit of the doubt because I may or may not love him, but evidence isn’t evidence until it’s actually evidence, you know?
: This really could just be mass hysteria at the end of the day. Regardless of the parade of red flags following him wherever he goes.
: Then there’s only one thing we can do.
: Yeah? And what’s that?
: We get that horse to open its mouth and speak.
: What?
: We say, “Horse. Talk.” Then we point at the elephant in the room and wait for him to ride it outta there.
: Okay, so you want to make him fess up. Got it. How, though? Because the closest I’ve come involved me dressing up like a schoolgirl and I’m not about to let you borrow my outfit.
: That’s easy, Imani. So easy that people have been relying on it since the dawn of time.
: You don’t mean...
: We get him really drunk and wait for him to slip up!
: Oh, cool. Mission text.
